richText: A controller reads HTTP input and chooses the HTTP response.
A service performs application operations and applies application rules.
A repository reads or writes stored data.
These are separate responsibilities. A simple endpoint does not need a service and repository if it has no application operation or stored data.
Servlet filters run before the controller. Spring Security uses filters when configured.
Spring MVC selects a controller method using the request mapping.
The controller calls the service. The service calls the repository when it needs stored data.
The result returns through the service to the controller. A message converter writes the response body.
Transaction boundaries belong around the operation that needs atomic database work, often a service method. The data-access lessons explain transactions.
